note: Scan artifacts carried in from the book these biographies were transcribed from, reported with batch 141 and repaired here. Three classes, each verified against the stored text before being written: the three records named in that flag, word-splits left by end-of-line hyphenation, and section headings captured onto the end of a biography. Every replacement is a literal string, matched exactly once, and the script reports each as applied or already done rather than rewriting anything blind.

not_attempted.class: Words run together, such as 'amember' or 'Hemade'
not_attempted.reason: This class cannot be detected safely. Searching the whole archive for rare long tokens that split into two common words returns 247 candidates across 342 records, and inspection shows the great majority are ordinary words the test happens to fit — unnamed, southeast, farmworkers, storefront, codefendant. There is no threshold that separates them from the real damage without a dictionary, so only the specific joins in the three named records are repaired. The rest wants an eye, not a regular expression.
